evals.prompt: Our `AGENTS.md` has grown to 450 lines. It copies the full `package.json` scripts table, lists the directory tree, has three different places explaining how database migrations work, and includes a 90-line deployment checklist that only matters during release cuts. Refactor it using `writing-for-agents` principles.
evals.expected_output: A refactored `AGENTS.md` plan and text that removes cached environment lookups (`package.json` scripts and directory tree), consolidates migration guidance into one co-located section (single source of truth), moves the branch-specific 90-line release checklist behind a sharp context pointer, and removes no-op filler.
expectations: Removes the copied `package.json` scripts and directory tree because the environment already serves as the source of truth
Co-locates the scattered database migration rules in one authoritative place instead of repeating them
Pushes the release-only deployment checklist out of `AGENTS.md` behind a context pointer with front-loaded trigger branches
Replaces negative prohibitions where possible with positive target instructions and cuts no-op sentences

evals.prompt: We are authoring a new `SKILL.md` for database schema migrations. Should it be model-invoked or user-invoked, how should we write its `description` pointer, and how do we prevent the agent from rushing past the safety-check step to generate the SQL file?
evals.expected_output: Guidance grounded in `writing-for-agents` and `references/skill-mechanics.md` covering the model-invoked vs. user-invoked trade-off (context load vs. cognitive load), a front-loaded description with one trigger per distinct branch, and a checkable, exhaustive completion criterion on the safety-check step.
expectations: Explains the trade-off between model-invoked (permanent context load via description) and user-invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`, cognitive load)
Writes a context pointer description that front-loads trigger words and avoids synonym repetition for the same branch
Defines a sharp, checkable, exhaustive completion criterion on the safety-check step before considering splitting the sequence across a context boundary
